thread:
chiara: ok folks, pushed an nsys capture for the tail spikes we saw in production yesterday. link: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/nsys/2061122334.qdrep
kevin: grabbing it now. quick summary of what I saw in the flame: huge CPU time in the TRTEngine wrapper (~200ms slices), scheduler loop shows a lot of small wake/sleep cycles, and kernel launches are fragmented (lots of cudaLaunchKernel calls).
ryan: can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll try a couple of runs with sampling.
chiara: ran with:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_2061122334 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --force-overwrite --stats=true --capture-range=cuda:runtime
```
chiara: main observations from the capture: wrapper CPU (pre/post invoke) ~210ms, scheduler handling (dequeue+policy) ~120ms, kernel execution aggregates ~340ms, cudaMemcpyAsync peaks ~85-95ms. lots of tiny kernels named like `trt_invoke_slice` and a fallback `generic_attention_kernel`.
kevin: that fallback is suspicious. looks like TRT selected a safe generic kernel for attention on >512 seq lengths. when that happens register pressure spikes and things slow down. any evidence of plugin fallback in logs?
chiara: yes NVTX spans show `TrtSelectKernel: fallback` around the same timestamps. Also saw repeated kernel symbol name changes which aligns with kernel auto-selection.
ryan: I ran a quick compare locally with env toggles: `TRT_FORCE_FAST_ATTENTION=1` (forces optimized kernel) => kernel time down ~30%, but memcpy time increased ~10% (maybe due to different memory layout). overall p99 latency dropped ~15%.
sasha: interesting, so we trade memcpy overhead for faster compute. do we have Batching heuristics that could avoid long seqs getting bundled with short ones? that would prevent slow-path being chosen mid-batch.
kevin: yep, current batcher groups by arrival time and then tries to fill to a token budget. it doesn't split on seq length variance. proposal: add a lightweight bucketing pass: group candidates by max_seq_len bucket before filling. should be cheap and reduce mixed batches.
chiara: also KV-cache: I noticed prefetch isn't firing for resumed conversations. trace shows KV warmup calls, but many hit the scheduler again (cold path). header `X-KV-Cache: hit` missing on several requests. maybe a race in the cache registration step during attach.
ryan: I instrumented the attach path yesterday. in high load, attach calls can be reordered behind the scheduler ack because we use optimistic enqueue + async attach. small window where scheduler sees sequence without cache -> triggers prewarm shell.
sasha: small fix idea: make attach synchronous for the first request of a session id or mark as high-priority attach. cheap to try.
kevin: for immediate triage we should: 1) reproduce with deterministic microbenchmark (seqs 64/128/512/1024 mixed), 2) run nsys with per-thread CPU sampling and per-kernel timing, 3) try `TRT_FORCE_FAST_ATTENTION=1` toggle and run with new bucketing.
chiara: I started a microbenchmark script and uploaded it: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/perf/microbench_2061122334.tar.gz (contains driver, payloads). will share results here.
chiara: sample raw numbers from one run (mixed batch of 64/512):
```
wrapper_cpu: 210ms
scheduler_cpu: 120ms
kernels_total: 340ms
 - trt_fast_attention: 120ms (if forced)
 - generic_attention_kernel: 320ms (fallback)
memcpy_async: 90ms
end-to-end p99: 780ms
```
ryan: thanks. that matches my local toggles. forcing fast attention improves kernel time significantly. we need to be careful about correctness/accuracy tradeoffs though. we should run evals to check output parity.
sasha: I'll own the bucketing change. will add a config flag and gate it behind `experimental.batcher_length_buckets`. I'll also add a small unit test to ensure stable ordering.
kevin: I'll take the TRT side: add a debug env that prints kernel selection reasons in the engine (only in dev builds) so we can correlate selection -> trace. also will try a patch to lower the cost of fast kernel when seq_len=1024 (tune tile sizes).
chiara: action items:
 - sasha: implement length bucketing + perf run (ETA EOD PT)
 - kevin: add selection debug logs + perf run (ETA tomorrow AM)
 - ryan: run eval parity test on forced-fast-attn images (ETA tomorrow)
 - chiara: run CI nsys captures (sampled) across prod-sim load and upload artifacts to the perf bucket
devops-bot: artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-perf/nsys/2061122334/trace_2061122334.qdrep (uploaded by chiara) :white_check_mark:
kevin: one more note: scheduler small-wake pattern looks like we call `notify_one()` per ready request rather than `notify_all()` then steal; that causes many context switches. I'll prototype batching notifications (coalesce up to N signals) to reduce wakeups.
ryan: sounds good. also consider using thread-local spare pools for KV buffers to cut memcpy costs.
chiara: for reproducibility: please run with these envs when testing: `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=1 TRACING_NVTX=1 TRT_FORCE_FAST_ATTENTION=<0|1> REDWOOD_BUCKETER=length_v1`. add `--nsys-sample-cpu` to trace command.
sasha: got it. I'll post results when I have first pass numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: assigning a follow-up thread after we have microbench numbers to discuss longer-term fixes (kernel tuning + batching heuristics).
chiara: cool, closing this thread for now. I'll reopen with the upload link to the filtered perfetto flame and a short annotated screenshot.
